full_judgment:
3. The plaintiff appellant claims that be is the Mutwalli of the Wakf Estate of Nazre-Mahmuda. The said Wakf Estate is the owner of the suit plot No. 23 comprising 2.15 acres and appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 48 of mouza Bagumbari District Dhaka. As Mutwalli the plaintiff is also the owner of two huts thereon. The defendant No. 2 took monthly lease of the suit land from the plaintiff in 1958 on a rental of Rs. 300/-, per month in the name of the defendant No. M/S. National Saw Mill. Defendant No. 3 was disclosed as the partner of the defendant No. 2 in the business Defendant No. 2 paid rent upto August, 1959 and thereafter stopped payment. The plaintiff came to know that the defendant No. 2 had sublet the suit land to the defendant Nos. 4. without the know ledge and consent of the plaintiff. The defendants are making preparation for construction of new huts modeling or repairing old huts and planting of new machineries which actions are illegal and prejudicial to the plaintiff. Hence the suit for permanent injunction. 

 6. Both the Courts have concurrently held that the plaintiff's story of ownership of the suit property as Mutwalli of the Wakf Estate of Nazre Mahmuda is totally unsubstantiated. Both the Courts found that the plaintiff is in forcible and adverse possession. The trial Courts, however, found that the khatian of C.S. khatian No. 48 stands in the name of Bishi Bewa. Suit plot No. 23 is in possession of Nabu Bepari by way of purchase. Nabu Bepari transferred the suit plot to Hem Nalini Gulfa by a registered sale deed of which the certified copy is Ext. 7 dated 10.9.1918. The trial Court held that Bishi Bewa did not have possession in suit plot No. 23 after the C.S. operation. Therefore, her grand-daughters Victoria and Eliz could not have settled the suit plot with the defendant Nos. 4 and 5. The trial Court also found from the evidence on record that the plaintiff constructed the two huts in question. Ext. 5 is the photostat copy of the agreement dated 18.2.58 and it shows that defendant No. 2 hired the said huts from the plaintiff and paid advance rent. He also paid regular rent as is shown from the counterfoils of rent receipts Ext. 4 series. The trial Court did not place any reliance on the papers filed by the defendants. It held that in spite of the fact that the plaintiff has not acquired any good title to the suit land, be can maintain a suit for permanent injunction against others who do not have a better title than him. He found that Hem Nalini has instituted Title Suit No. 27 of 1960 in the 1st Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for establishment of title and khas possession of suit plot No. 23 and other plots. He granted permanent injection to the plaintiff title the final decision of the said Title Suit No. 27 of 1960.
